0.why: OSC_WaveMorph_3.cpp:641 clamps this voltage to 0 to 8V and raises two to it, so it tracks one volt per octave over that span; unpatched it reads 4V

1.why: OSC_WaveMorph_3.cpp:614 clamps this voltage divided by five to plus or minus 1, reading the first channel only

2.why: OSC_WaveMorph_3.cpp:651 divides this voltage by ten into the cutoff; unpatched it reads 10V

3.why: OSC_WaveMorph_3.cpp:551 divides this voltage by ten into the resonance; unpatched it reads 10V

4.why: OSC_WaveMorph_3.cpp:656 divides this voltage by ten into the level; unpatched it reads 10V

5.why: OSC_WaveMorph_3.cpp:624 passes it to a SchmittTrigger, which fires above 1V, reading the first channel only

comment: The panel prints -10V, 0V and 10V beside the Morph input, but the code divides that input by 5, so the first and third waveforms are reached at -5V and 5V. Draw, Solo, Invert, Presets, Rand and Copy are custom widgets rather than parameters.
